about: Popcorn eval cases. A point is kept when one surviving popcorn matches its topic and every detail group (each a list of alternatives, case-insensitive regular expressions). Typed cases are invented; the Millbrook cases are the invented sample conversations in packages/samples.

cases.title: A typed submission with four digested points (stand-in until the real text arrives)
cases.text:
Four things I want the council to hear before the vote.
First, do it street by street, not house by house. When the whole of Quarry Row is done in one go the scaffolding and the trench are shared, and the builders told us that takes about a quarter off the cost of each house.
Second, stop sending letters. Half my street puts anything with the council crest straight in the recycling. What got my mother to sign up for the insulation survey was the electrician from number eight knocking on her door and showing her his own meter.
Third, renters need protection written into the scheme, not a promise. My landlord has ignored the mould in our back bedroom for two winters. If the street scheme is voluntary for landlords, tenants like me will be the last ones still on gas in 2035, and then we pay the rent rise after the refit.
Fourth, keep the pool warm. The Mell Valley pool is the only place the older people on Linden Terrace exercise in winter. If the river heat network cannot promise the water stays at 29 degrees, say so before the vote, not after.

points.says: Do whole streets at once; shared scaffolding takes a quarter off each house
Letters go in the recycling; a neighbour at the door works
Renters need protection in the scheme or they are last on gas
Promise the pool stays at 29 degrees before the vote

cases.title: A typed submission whose point needs more than twelve words
cases.text: The last bus back to Thornby Hollow leaves Market Square at 6pm, so anyone up there without a car cannot come to the evening sessions at the Weavers' Hall. Hold at least one session on a Saturday morning, or run a minibus. Otherwise the hamlet that is off the gas grid, and has the most to lose from all this, is the one that is never in the room.

points.says: The last bus leaves at 6pm, so people without a car miss evening sessions
Hold a Saturday morning session or run a minibus
The off-grid hamlet with the most to lose is never in the room
A heat pump quote of 14,800 leaves nine thousand out of a nurse's pocket
Four thousand of frozen stock at risk; nobody pays for lost trade
Whole streets at once knock 20 to 25 percent off
A subsidised refit then a 200 a month rent rise puts renters out
Council letters get binned; a neighbour who explains works
A demonstration house with real bills on a cold January day
An 80 percent sign-up threshold earns the whole street a bonus
Six weeks without heat waiting for a part; local repair within 48 hours
Voluntary or mandatory: the unresolved divide
Mandatory standards for landlords, incentives for owner occupiers

cases.title: Millbrook trades table: delivery and skills

points.says: Twelve thousand of gas spares become scrap
Pay the day rate while trades retrain, like jury service
Sixty amp fuses need 1,500 to 2,000 of electrical work first
A dead combi is fixed the same day; a heat pump takes three weeks
Ring-fence the work for local trades, not out-of-town contractors
4,500 of tooling and a new van before the first job
Ten years of steady work, not nine-month voucher schemes
Reinforce the grid street by street before any mandate; no 700 fee on one home
Eighty percent of apprentice places sit with small gas firms
Respect what the trades already know about these houses
